title: Basic Commands [chmod]
description:
# chmod
`chmod` stands for `change mode`. It allows you to change who can read, write, and execute files. There are 2 ways to use chmod, A: by number, and B: by specifics.
A: by number.
Each value has a number associated with it:
- r (read): 4
- w (write): 2
- x (execute): 1
- none: 0
To get a permission, you can us adding them together, so everything is 7 (rwx), or read and execute (rx) is 5. Then, you can combine your 3 values: owner (file creator default), group (i will explain later), everyone (any user on the computer), so for the owner to have all permissions (`rwx`), the group to have read and execute (`r-x`), and all people to have read-only (`r--`) (combined `rwxr-xr--`) would be 754. Then, you would `chmod NUMBER filepath`.
### By specifics
By specifics is simple. To adjust somthing, you do `chmod SPECIFIER+/-VALUE FILEPATH`. SPECIFIER can be 4 things:
- `u`: user (you),
- `g`: your group (again, later),
- `o`: others (anyone else)
- `a`: all 3.
+ = add permission, and - = remove permission.
IDENTIFIER = a combination of r, w, and x (read write and execute), so to add read and write to group, you would run `chmod g+rw PATH`.
